SST on Renovation & Construction Malaysia (2026): When to Charge 6%

Published 19 November 2026

Since 1 July 2025, construction work services in Malaysia are taxed at 6%, but only contractors registered for service tax charge it. You must register once your taxable construction work exceeds RM1.5 million in 12 months, and work on residential buildings is excluded. So most small contractors renovating homes don’t add SST, while larger contractors doing shops, offices and other commercial work usually must. Here’s how it works and how to show it on a quotation.

This guide is general information, not tax advice. The rules changed several times in 2025 and 2026, so confirm your own position with your tax agent or the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD).

The rules at a glance

Item Rule
Tax Service tax on construction work services (Group L)
Rate 6%
From 1 July 2025
Registration threshold More than RM1.5 million of taxable construction work services in 12 months
Residential buildings Excluded, including related public facilities
Completed residential buildings Exempt under Service Tax Policy 2/2026 (18 June 2026), backdated to 1 July 2025
Commercial and industrial work Taxable if you’re registered
Government projects Federal, state and local authorities are exempt from paying it, with supporting documents

Do you need to charge SST? Three questions

  1. Are you registered for service tax under Group L? If not, you don’t charge it, and you mustn’t show SST on your quotation or invoice.
  2. Does your taxable work exceed RM1.5 million in 12 months? If so, you need to register. Only taxable work counts: excluded residential work doesn’t, as long as your documents show why it’s excluded.
  3. Is this job taxable? For a registered contractor, work on a shop, office, factory or other non-residential building is generally taxable. Work on a residential building isn’t.

Renovating homes: the residential exclusion

Construction of residential buildings and related public facilities is outside the tax. In June 2026, RMCD issued Service Tax Policy 2/2026, which exempts construction work on completed residential buildings, meaning renovation of existing homes, with effect from 1 July 2025. Registered contractors who had already charged service tax on this work could claim a refund, after first refunding their customers.

Keep documents that show the property is residential, and put the client’s name and the property address on your quotation and invoice.

Mixed developments and shophouses

When one job covers both residential and commercial space, only the non-residential part is taxable. Split it using the contract, drawings and bill of quantities. Where the values can’t be separated, a wider amount may end up being taxed, so itemise from the start.

Materials vs labour on your invoice

Service tax applies to the construction work service. RMCD’s guidance allows materials to be listed separately, at actual cost with supplier invoices to support them, so that tax applies only to the service portion. If your invoice is a lump sum that doesn’t separate goods from services, the whole amount may be taxed.

For a registered contractor on a commercial job, that’s a strong reason to quote and invoice by line item, not as one lump sum.

How to show SST on a quotation

If you’re not registered (most small renovation contractors):

  • Don’t add a service tax line, and don’t write “SST included”.
  • Your total is simply your price.

If you’re registered and the job is taxable:

  • Show your SST registration number on your invoices, and ideally on the quotation too.
  • Show the subtotal, the service tax at 6% and the total including tax as separate lines.
  • If you list materials separately, keep them at cost and keep the supplier invoices.

If you’re registered but the job is residential:

  • Leave the tax at 0%, and keep the documents that show the property is residential.

Our free renovation quotation template has a service tax line set to 0% by default, with a dropdown for 6% when you need it.

Contracts signed before the tax started

Contracts signed before the tax started, with no price review clause and stamped by the deadline, are exempt until 30 June 2027. From 1 July 2027, work under those contracts becomes taxable. If you have a long-running contract from before July 2025, check the exact conditions with your tax agent.

Quotations are not invoices

A quotation isn’t submitted to LHDN’s MyInvois system, and service tax is accounted for on your invoices, not your quotes. But showing the tax correctly on the quotation avoids a nasty surprise for the client when the invoice arrives. Frequently asked questions

Is renovation work subject to SST in Malaysia?
It can be. Since 1 July 2025, construction work services, including renovation that forms part of construction work, are taxable at 6%. But only contractors registered for service tax charge it, and work on residential buildings is excluded. Most small contractors renovating homes therefore don't charge SST.
When does a contractor have to register for service tax?
When the value of taxable construction work services exceeds RM1.5 million in a 12-month period. Excluded residential work doesn't count towards the threshold, but you need documents that show why it's excluded.
Do I charge SST on a shop or office renovation?
If you're registered for service tax under Group L, generally yes: commercial fit-outs aren't covered by the residential exclusion. Separate repair or maintenance contracts may fall under a different group, so check how the work is classified with your tax agent.
Is service tax charged on materials?
Service tax applies to the value of the construction work service. If you list materials separately from the service on the invoice, at cost, the tax applies to the service portion. If the invoice is a lump sum that can't be separated, the whole amount may be taxed.
